sections.title: Scope and evidence baseline
sections.text:
Date: 2026-10-10. Code baseline: `main`, `09612160c98ca6133c894a8f90f5653b9dac6b8f` (0.7.0, tag `v0.7.0`).
Repository HEAD `47105c3` only adds plan files and un-ignores `/plans/`; `git diff 0961216 HEAD -- packages tests bin
.github composer.json` is empty, so every code anchor below is valid for both commits.

Status: **architecture revision 2**. Revision 1 was authored by Codex (GPT-6 family). Revision 2 is the result of an
independent architecture review by Claude Opus 5.5 against the code, the earlier audit ideas and current primary
sources. The review record, every material change and its reason are in `#review`; replaced decisions are kept
through the protocol (`supersedes`/`superseded_by`). Implementation has not started.

This design fixes the target boundaries, ownership, extension contracts, operation chains, persistence rules,
compatibility policy and release conditions. The transition is four ordered phase skeletons; separate sessions
detail one phase at a time. This is redistribution of existing behavior, not a feature expansion.

Inputs: [architecture ideas](../../../../audits/2026-10-09-architecture-modularization.md),
[completed hardening](../../../../audits/2026-10-09-audit.md),
[consistency implementation](../../../../audits/2026-10-09-consistency-design.md),
[roadmap](../../../../ROADMAP.md), [changelog](../../../../CHANGELOG.md), both API manifests, the source code, the
CI workflows and the ecosystem packages CoreX, Chatom, Commerz and Vaulter. The earlier audit supplies the starting
ideas; decisions here rest on the current implementation.

Reading order for a phase-design session: `#product` → `#ownership` → `#scope-boundary` → `#extension-system` →
`#spi-catalog` → `#operation-chains` → `#persistence` → `#api-compatibility` → `#invariants` → `#release-gate` →
`#transition-policy`. `#cost`, `#risks` and `#review` explain trade-offs; `#evidence` lists anchors and sources.
The reference documents `knowledge/type-map`, `knowledge/target-structure`, `knowledge/contracts`,
`knowledge/identities` and `knowledge/upgrade-map` turn these rules into an exhaustive, per-symbol standard; phase
detail may refine but never contradict them without a plan amendment.

sections.title: The product we are building
sections.text:
**One small authorization engine, explicit optional modules, independently useful integration packages.**
The engine owns the meaning and safety of an access decision and of an authority write. Modules supply behavior
through that meaning; they never supply a second engine. Public names and persistent identities belong to these
logical boundaries, not to the directory or Composer archive that currently contains them.

There are three different notions of size:

| Dimension | Target |
|:--|:--|
| What an application must understand | One panel, permission enums, code roles, a subject, grant/revoke and check/authorize. Tenancy, assignment scopes, journals and extension contracts are additional guides. |
| What a basic application executes | The common decision/write path and only its selected sources. No optional-module query, listener, table, handler instantiation or console registration outside the console. |
| What is distributed | `axiomasoft/azguard` (core + internal modules) and `axiomasoft/azguard-filament`. A new Composer package requires an independent purpose outside AzGuard internals. |

Separation follows responsibility, never monetization. No edition switch, alternative decision rule, second schema
or name such as "pro" enters the code. A self-contained integration (Filament today) may later have its own
distribution or license; an internal module is built so that relocating its files is a packaging operation that
changes no API, schema or data — whether it is ever relocated is an owner distribution decision outside this design.

Lightweight never means removing safety. Tenant identity, expiry, consistent authority reads, validation,
fail-closed decisions and one guarded write path are present whenever the corresponding data is used. Optional
modules add no work when inactive; shared identity columns and core value types stay available.

### Fixed decisions (revision 2)

1. Core keeps tenant isolation, request context and the **assignment-scope algebra**: scope identities, the closed
   mode vocabulary, the applicability envelope and structural verification. Scope **behavior** (rich definitions,
   eligibility filters, adapters, membership, directories, exact eligibility queries) is the Scopes module (D7).
2. Scopes behavior, Audit and DevTools (generators and onboarding scaffolding) are internal modules with their own
   autoload roots and composition; Filament stays the only separate package (D6, D7).
3. Standard source adapters (Database, Folder, Gate, Relation) stay in core and are selected explicitly. Authority
   writes belong to core storage only; third-party sources are read sources (D10).
4. One decision engine, one visibility compiler, one write coordinator. Every extension output is a candidate,
   a veto, a narrowing or an observation that core verifies; none is a final allow (D8).
5. A plugin is a pure per-panel declaration: `id()` and `register()`. Contributions are typed, ordered,
   deterministic and sealed before requests run. No `boot()`, no plugin-ID dependency, no macros (D8).
6. Modules and Filament interact only through core contracts and core values: no sibling imports, bridges,
   plugin-ID checks, shared module tables or `class_exists()` switches (D7).
7. The frozen surface is the real consumer and implementer surface, marked with typed ecosystem attributes and
   including members, overrides, named arguments, enums, data formats and persistence (D4, D9).
8. The separation completes before 1.0; a later physical relocation preserves FQCNs, configuration, commands,
   events, migration identities and data (D6).

sections.title: Exact ownership and target layout
sections.text:
"Core" is a set of responsibilities inside the base package, not one giant public namespace. Implementations are
organized by responsibility and hidden behind a small supported surface. Do not manufacture a Composer package or
an interface for each core service.

| Responsibility | Owner | What stays there |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Domain values | Core `Kernel` | Permission/role keys, subject/actor/tenant references, `AccessScope`, `AssignmentScopeRef`, `AnyAssignmentScope`, decisions, contribution witnesses, predicate vocabulary. Pure PHP. FQCNs unchanged (they may be serialized by hosts). |
| Extension language | Core `Contracts/<domain>` | Only contracts with a core caller: sources, hooks, restrictions, conditions, change pipes and participants, plugins, scope definitions and evaluators, resource/request resolvers, directories, diagnostics. Catalogue in `#spi-catalog`. |
| Declarations and catalogs | Core `Panels`, `Catalog`, `Roles`, `Permissions`, `Policies`, `Schema` | Panel DSL (`PanelBuilder`), code permissions/roles, policy declarations, neutral schema descriptors, compiled catalogs, typed per-panel module options. |
| Request context | Core `Context` | Current `AccessScope` (read), validated scoped execution, `AssignmentScopePhase`, `AssignmentScopeRuntime`, model→context mapping from declared scope types. Panel/Fiber locality. |
| Tenant isolation | Core `Tenancy` | `TenantPolicy`, `ModelTenantDefinition`, tenant membership restriction, tenant resolver/directory/membership contracts, global-tenant roles. No AzGuard tenant table. |
| Assignment-scope algebra | Core `Context` + `Contracts/Scopes` | Closed `AssignmentScopeMode`, the single scope declaration slot, applicability envelope, structural verification, role scope types, neutral scope contracts (`#scope-boundary`). |
| Decision execution | Core `Authorization` | Mandatory stage graph, source aggregation, expiry, super-admin, policy evaluation, restrictions, batch orchestration, exact query composition, guarded candidate queries. |
| Authority persistence and writes | Core `Storage`, `Changes`, `Sources/Database` | Six authority tables, revisions/epoch, snapshots, locks, the only authority writer, validated changes, change events built once, participant invocation, after-commit publication, storage descriptor and identity-column schema helper. No audit table. |
| Standard read adapters | Core `Sources/{Database,Folder,Gate,Relation}` | Existing storage, discovery, native Gate and relation-backed sources. Their panel binding is core-internal preparation, not a public lifecycle SPI. |
| Host/UI access | Core `Directories`, `Schema` | Subject/tenant directories, lookup values, delegation to declared scope directories, readonly descriptions including writer capabilities. |
| Framework and operations | Core `Laravel`, `Diagnostics`, `Configuration` | Gate bridge and its public result adapter, HTTP/queue lifecycle, doctor/explain, storage migration generator, authority maintenance, typed configuration. |
| Consumer testing | Core `Testing` | Fake mirroring `AzGuard\AzGuard`, consumer helpers, contract suites for core SPI. |
| Assignment-scope behavior | Internal module `AzGuard\Scopes` | `ScopesPlugin` DSL, model-backed definitions, filters, access adapters, scope membership, role-binding refinement, the evaluator, exact eligibility queries, default scope directory, `ContextAware` trait, scope doctor checks, module contract suites. Plugin only; no provider, table or config section. |
| Audit | Internal module `AzGuard\Audit` | `AuditPlugin`, typed options (retention), journal participant and row encoding, audit schema/migrations/adoption, per-storage migration generator, health/shape checks, retention/prune command. |
| Development tools | Internal module `AzGuard\DevTools` | `azguard:make:*`, `azguard:stubs`, onboarding `azguard:install`, scaffolding, code stubs and the `scaffold` config section. Console-only registration. |
| Filament | `axiomasoft/azguard-filament` | Resource authorization, list filtering, editors, pages, exports and Filament generators through supported core API/SPI and neutral descriptors only. |

```text
packages/core/                         axiomasoft/azguard
  composer.json                        psr-4: AzGuard\ → src/, AzGuard\Scopes\ → modules/scopes/src/,
                                              AzGuard\Audit\ → modules/audit/src/, AzGuard\DevTools\ → modules/devtools/src/
                                       laravel.providers: AzGuardServiceProvider, Audit\AuditServiceProvider,
                                              DevTools\DevToolsServiceProvider (distribution metadata, not a core import)
  config/azguard.php                   one package config file; sections owned as listed below
  database/migrations/                 the two existing core basenames only
  stubs/storage-migration.stub         core installation stub
  src/
    AzGuard.php                        typed application entry point (replaces AzGuardManager)
    AzGuardServiceProvider.php         core composition only
    Facades/AzGuard.php                Laravel adapter mirroring AzGuard\AzGuard
    Attributes/{Api,Spi,SpiKind}       publication markers (ecosystem convention)
    Kernel/ Contracts/<domain>/ Context/ Tenancy/
    Panels/ Catalog/ Roles/ Permissions/ Policies/ Schema/
    Authorization/ Changes/ Storage/ Sources/{Database,Folder,Gate,Relation}/
    Directories/ Events/ Exceptions/ Configuration/ Diagnostics/ Laravel/ Concerns/ Support/ Testing/
  modules/
    scopes/src/                        AzGuard\Scopes: ScopesPlugin, Contracts/, Definitions/, Internal/, Testing/
    audit/src/                         AzGuard\Audit: AuditPlugin, AuditOptions, AuditServiceProvider, Internal/
    audit/database/migrations/         audit create/adopt migration (published, fixed basename)
    audit/stubs/                       per-storage audit migration stub
    devtools/src/                      AzGuard\DevTools: DevToolsServiceProvider, Console/, Scaffold/
    devtools/stubs/                    code stubs
packages/filament/                     axiomasoft/azguard-filament
```

The exhaustive placement of every one of the 464 baseline types and 43 new types (owner, target FQCN, marker, action,
phase, reason) is `knowledge/type-map`; the resulting package and module trees, composer metadata, resources and test
ownership are `knowledge/target-structure`; normative signatures are `knowledge/contracts`. They follow one rule:
an attributed type lives outside `\Internal\`, an internal type lives under `<Zone>\Internal\` (D13).

`Contracts`, `Data`, `Enums`, `Events`, `Exceptions` and `Internal` are ownership categories, not compulsory empty
folders. Keep clear existing public names (`Panels\PanelBuilder`, `Changes\ChangeResult`, `Kernel\Identity\SubjectRef`).
Implementation classes move into `<Zone>\Internal` (D13); public wrappers keep their names. No `src/Scopes`, `src/Audit`,
`src/DevTools` or `src/Plugins/Audit` tree remains, so each FQCN has exactly one autoload owner.

### Namespace map of the mixed areas (single pre-1.0 transition)

| Current | Target | Owner |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `Scopes\{AssignmentScopePhase,AssignmentScopeRuntime}`; `Scopes\{CurrentContext,WithinContext}` | `Context\…`; `Context\Internal\…` (read through `PanelAccess::scope()`/`AzGuard::currentScope()`, run through `AzGuard::withinScope()`) | core |
| `Scopes\{TenantPolicy,ModelTenantDefinition}`; tenant part of `Scopes\MembershipRestriction`; `Contracts\Scopes\{TenantResolver,TenantMembership,TenantDirectory}` | `Tenancy\…`, `Contracts\Tenancy\…` | core |
| `Scopes\ModelIdentity` | tenant mapping → `Tenancy\Internal`; context mapping → `Context\Internal`; keys → existing `Support\ModelKey` | core |
| `Contracts\Scopes\{AssignmentScopeDefinition,QueryableAssignmentScopeDefinition,ResolvedAssignmentScope,ProvidesAccessScope,ProvidesAssignmentScope,ResourceScopeResolver,AssignmentScopeResolver,AssignmentScopeDirectory}` | unchanged FQCN | core |
| new: scope mode enum, scope declaration value, evaluator contracts, typed resource→context mapping contract | `Context\…`, `Contracts\Scopes\…` | core |
| `Scopes\Query\{PredicateBuilder,PredicateQuery,QueryGuard}` | `Authorization\Query\Internal` (generic guarded candidate query) | core |
| `Scopes\{AssignmentScopePolicy,BaseAssignmentScope,ModelAssignmentScopeDefinition,AssignmentScopeSettings,RoleBindings,ScopeConfiguration,ContextAware}`, `Scopes\Query\EligibilityBuilder` | module `AzGuard\Scopes\…` (policy DSL becomes `ScopesPlugin`) | Scopes |
| `Contracts\Scopes\{AssignmentScopeFilter,AssignmentScopeAccessAdapter,AssignmentScopeMembership,ConfigurableAssignmentScopeDefinition}` | `AzGuard\Scopes\Contracts\…` | Scopes |
| `Authorization\ScopeEligibility`, scope part of `Authorization\Query\VisibilityScope`, `Directories\QueryScopeDirectory`, scope part of `Diagnostics\Checks\MembershipConfigured` | module internals | Scopes |
| `Plugins\Audit\*`, `Changes\ChangeJournal`, `AuditPruneCommand`, audit DDL in `StorageSchema`, `DatabaseSource::appendJournal`, `ChangePipeline::pruneJournal`, audit entry of `StorageHealth` | `AzGuard\Audit\…` | Audit |
| `Laravel\Console\Commands\Make\*`, `Laravel\Console\Scaffold\*`, `StubsCommand`, `InstallCommand`, code stubs | `AzGuard\DevTools\…` (command names unchanged) | DevTools |
| `AzGuardManager` | `AzGuard\AzGuard` | core |
| `Plugins\BasePlugin`, `Plugins\PluginContext::dependencies()`, `Contracts\Plugins\DependsOnPlugins`, `Panels\GateMode`, SPI status of `Contracts\Sources\StoresGrants` | retired | — |

### Configuration and composition ownership

One package config file stays (ecosystem rule). Core owns every existing key except `scaffold.*`, which DevTools
owns. `defaults.scopes.resolvers` and `discovery.scopes` stay core keys because request resolvers and scope
definitions are core contracts. Audit retention and scope policies remain typed plugin options, not config keys.
A module registers its root section with core configuration validation from its own provider; core contains no
module literal and still rejects unknown root keys after all installed owners registered. Existing key paths do not
move, so published `config/azguard.php` files keep working; the only removed key is `defaults.gate.mode` (the
single-value `GateMode`), whose unknown-key error names the upgrade step.

Composition roots: `AzGuardServiceProvider` registers only core. `AuditServiceProvider` registers the prune and
audit-migration commands and the audit publish tag; it performs no I/O and activates nothing. `DevToolsServiceProvider`
registers commands and stub publishing only when running in console and owns the `scaffold` section. Scopes has no
provider. Panel attachment (`plugins([...])`) is the only runtime activation.

### Dependency map

```mermaid
flowchart BT
    K[Kernel values]
    C[Core contracts and shared values] --> K
    D[Panels, catalogs, schema] --> C
    R[Decision, visibility and write coordinators] --> C
    S[Storage and standard adapters] --> C
    L[Core Laravel composition] --> D
    L --> R
    L --> S
    SC[Scopes module] --> C
    SC --> D
    AU[Audit module] --> C
    AU --> D
    DT[DevTools module] --> C
    DT --> D
    FI[Filament package] --> C
    FI --> D
```

Inside core, explicitly owned implementation dependencies are allowed; Kernel purity and supported-signature closure
remain mandatory. Forbidden edges: core→module (imports, FQCN strings, class-strings, plugin IDs, module table names),
module→module, module/Filament→Filament/module, and any extension→core `Internal`/`@internal` symbol.

sections.title: Assignment scopes: core algebra, module behavior
sections.text:
The assignment scope is the hardest boundary: its identity is part of every grant row and request, while its rich
behavior is needed by only some applications. Revision 1 placed inheritance in the module behind one broad evaluator.
Revision 2 splits **algebra** (core) from **behavior** (module), because the algebra is interpreted over core-owned
columns in scalar, batch, SQL and write paths and must not depend on asking a module.

### What core owns: the algebra

| Element | Rule |
|:--|:--|
| Identity | `AccessScope{tenant, context}`, `AssignmentScopeRef`, `AnyAssignmentScope`, the `global` sentinel, `context_*` columns and reasons. Unchanged. |
| Mode vocabulary | Closed enum `AssignmentScopeMode` replacing the string modes: `None`, `Inherit`, `Isolated`, `Required`. |
| Declaration slot | One effective declaration per panel: mode, definitions (by alias), per-alias directories, optional evaluator class. Contributions from provider, plugins and `configurePanels()` merge with the existing precedence and conflict rules of `PanelCompiler::scopePolicy()/scopes()` (mode by precedence, definitions unioned with a sameness check, plugin-only mode conflicts rejected). `ScopesPlugin` is one contributor; an application or third-party plugin may contribute through core SPI. Request resolvers stay the existing `scopeResolvers()` slot and `defaults.scopes.resolvers`. No declaration means `None`; a declaration without an evaluator means structural eligibility only and no exact SQL. |
| Envelope | The set of stored scopes that may contribute to a request (`EvaluationFrame::sourceScopes`): the selected scope, plus the tenant-wide scope when the request context is non-global and the mode is not `Isolated`, plus global-tenant variants for declared global roles. Computed by core only. |
| Structural verification | For a non-global context: the alias is declared, `AssignmentScopeDefinition::resolve()` returns a scope whose ref and owner tenant equal the request, a returned record matches the declared model and canonical key. Done before any evaluator call. |
| Role scope types | `BaseRole::scopes()` keeps returning definitions; core compiles only aliases and `scopeRequired()`; a binding's extra configuration is opaque to core and passed through to the evaluator. |
| Write admission frame | Mode checks, declared alias, role binding by alias, structural verification, then the evaluator; revocation, expiry and touch never consult the evaluator (current behavior), so removing scope behavior never blocks cleanup. |
| Typed resource mapping | `ProvidesAccessScope`, `ProvidesAssignmentScope`, `ResourceScopeResolver` and a new typed contract replacing the `method_exists(azguardContextType/azguardContextRelation)` probe. The `ContextAware` trait that implements it is module convenience. |

| Mode | Global request context | Non-global request context | Tenant-wide grants inside a scoped request |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `None` (default, no declaration) | allowed | denied `assignment_scope_not_accepted`; write rejected | — |
| `Inherit` | allowed | allowed for declared aliases | apply |
| `Isolated` | allowed | allowed for declared aliases | do not apply |
| `Required` | denied `assignment_scope_required`; write rejected | allowed for declared aliases | apply |

The role of folder-discovered `Scopes/` classes (collected by `PanelDiscovery` today) is verified in P1; whatever it is,
discovery cannot create a scope type outside the declaration.

A source may mark a contribution as applying in every context (today `#[GrantedToAll]` folder grants); core reads a
neutral property of the contribution value instead of `instanceof FolderSource`.

### What the module owns: behavior

Model-backed definitions (`BaseAssignmentScope`, `ModelAssignmentScopeDefinition`), configurable filters and their
settings, access adapters for external scope types, scope membership, role-binding refinement, the evaluator, the
exact eligibility query, the default scope directory, the `ContextAware` trait, owner/membership doctor warnings and
the plugin DSL. Everything a scope type needs beyond identity and envelope lives here.

### Evaluator SPI

| Contract | Purpose | Called by | Input → output | Core verification | Failure |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `AssignmentScopeEvaluator::validate` | compile-time validation of each declared definition and each role binding of that alias (today `ScopeConfiguration` called from `RoleCompiler`) | panel compiler, role compiler | definition + registered definition → void | none; it may only reject | `DefinitionException` at boot |
| `AssignmentScopeEvaluator::allows` | eligibility of one verified scope for one runtime (phase Access common/contribution, Assignment, Inspection) | Boundary and Restriction stages, write validator, directory filtering | `AssignmentScopeRuntime` + `ResolvedAssignmentScope` → bool | called only after structural verification; result can only narrow | access: deny `assignment_scope_filter_error` (distinguishable failure); write: `AssignmentScopeNotAcceptedException` with cause |
| `AssignmentScopeEvaluator::allowsMany` | the same answers for a decision set | batch preparation | list of runtime/resolved pairs → map by stable key | missing or extra key fails the set closed | the set fails as a unit |
| `QueryableAssignmentScopeEvaluator::eligibleContexts` (optional capability) | exact SQL equivalent of `allows` for one branch | visibility compiler | runtime + declared queryable definition + isolated guarded candidate query → narrowed context-key query | same model and connection, narrowing-only guard, core joins it to the resource branch and applies tenant/OR/AND guards | absent capability or `unsupported` → `VisibilityNotSupportedException` with a stable reason; never approximate |

Directories stay the existing `AssignmentScopeDirectory` contract, contributed per alias. The default model directory
is module code; a declared alias without a directory has an empty directory, so a UI cannot offer it and the write
path still revalidates anything submitted.

The evaluator is resolved from the container per operation; it reads its settings from the panel's typed module
options carried by the runtime's `Panel`, never from an application-wide binding overwritten by another panel.

### Call sites that change, and what they call

| Core path today | Target |
|:--|:--|
| `BoundaryStage::{decide,structural}` string modes, `scopeDefinition()`, `ScopeEligibility::common` | mode enum + declaration; structural verification; `allows(phase Access, role null)` |
| `EvaluationFrame::sourceScopes` (`'isolated'`) | envelope from mode enum |
| `ScopeEligibility::contribution`, `RoleBindings` | `allows(phase Access, role + contribution)`; bindings are refined inside the module |
| `MembershipRestriction` | tenant membership stays a core restriction; scope membership becomes a module restriction (with `FiltersAccessQueries` for SQL) |
| `Visibility::mapping`, `VisibilityScope`, `EligibilityBuilder` | typed resource→context mapping (core); `eligibleContexts` (module); core composition |
| `ChangeValidator::{tenancy,eligibility,scopeMember}` | mode enum + structural verification + `allows(phase Assignment, proposed values)` |
| `DirectoryResolver::scopes`, `QueryScopeDirectory` | declared directory per alias; module default |
| `PanelAdmission::holdsRole`, `WithinContext`, `ModelIdentity::context`, `RoleCompiler`, `SchemaBuilder` | declaration and definitions only (aliases, models, labels); no module class |
| `PanelRegistry` binding of `RelationSource` | core-internal preparation from the declaration; `RelationSource` stays a core read adapter that requires a declared queryable alias and fails compilation otherwise |
| `Diagnostics\Checks\MembershipConfigured` | tenant part core; scope part module doctor check |

### Disabled, absent or changed scope behavior

Removing `ScopesPlugin` from a panel leaves stored scoped rows untouched. The panel becomes `None`: non-global
requests are denied, scoped rows cannot match a global request scope, writes in a non-global context are rejected,
and revocation/expiry still work. Changing `Inherit` to `Isolated` only narrows. Changing a type alias is an identity
change (stored `context_type`), not a refactoring. Two panels may declare different modes and types; each compiled
declaration and its options are panel-local.

sections.title: The extension system
sections.text:
### Installation, availability, activation, execution

These are separate states. Autoloading makes code installed. A provider makes commands, publish tags and config
sections available. Attaching a plugin to a panel activates its declarations for that panel only. The engine executes
only the compiled contributions of that panel. Provider discovery never activates Audit or Scopes.

### Plugin SPI (revision 2)

```text
interface Plugin            #[Spi(kind: Implement)]
    id(): string            stable vendor/name id; azguard/* reserved for this package
    register(PanelBuilder $panel, PluginContext $context): void
```

- `register()` only declares through `PanelBuilder`; no database/network I/O, no current user/tenant/request/clock,
  no global listener. Nested `plugins([...])` from a plugin keeps the existing deterministic queue order.
- `boot()` is retired: no production plugin uses it (tests only observe it), it is a second lifecycle route that
  core cannot keep side-effect free, and Chatom/Commerz plugins are declaration-only. `BasePlugin` (an empty
  `boot()`) is retired with it. An implementation that still declares `boot()` compiles and is never called; the
  upgrade map says so.
- `DependsOnPlugins` and `PluginContext::dependencies()` are retired (owner principle 4). A contribution's
  requirements are implied by the slot and checked by core: a change participant requires the panel's core writer,
  `RelationSource` requires a declared queryable scope alias, the scope declaration merges by layer without conflicts. No separate
  "requires capability" API is added.
- `PluginContext` keeps `panelId()`, `pluginId()` and `buildId()`; keeping the parameter avoids a signature break for
  every existing plugin.
- Precedence stays the documented provider → plugins → `configurePanels()` → config defaults, with
  `withoutPlugins()` only on provider/configure layers. No priority sorting.

### Contribution slots

Every slot has one named contract. Objects implementing it or its class-string are accepted; a closure is accepted
only for a single-method contract and its parameter/return types are checked against that method at compilation.
Duck typing (`method_exists(handle)`) and invocation by parameter name (`RuntimeInvoker` passing `request`/`context`)
are removed. Class-strings are resolved per operation through the container.

| Slot | Contract | Arity | Authority and failure rule |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Permission/role/grant/policy sources | existing `Contracts\Sources\Provides*`, `FencesReads`, `FiltersQueries`, `DescribesSchema`, `ChecksHealth` | ordered list | Supply definitions or candidates. Core validates panel, tenant, envelope, origin, expiry and provenance; a source cannot emit a final allow. Exceptions fail the decision (`source_error`/`consistency_error`). |
| Policies | existing policy bindings and native Gate | per permission | Core preserves authority modes and evaluates outcomes in the mandatory pipeline. |
| Before hooks | `BeforeHook` (new name for the existing slot) → `BeforeResult{Continue,Deny}` | ordered list | Veto or continue only; cannot skip Boundary or create authority. Exception → failed decision. SQL requires `FiltersAccessQueries`. |
| Restrictions | existing `Restriction` (+ optional `FiltersAccessQueries`) | ordered list, unique key | Narrow only; exception → failure, never a silently absent restriction. |
| Grant conditions | existing `GrantCondition` | ordered list | Qualify one contribution; narrow only. |
| After hooks | `AfterHook` (new name for the existing slot) | ordered list | Observe the produced decision; existing failure isolation preserved; no replacement. |
| Change pipes | `ChangePipe` (new name for the existing duck-typed slot) | ordered list | Transform `until`/fields or cancel by throwing; guarded continuation exactly once; core final validation after the last pipe; the writer's result cannot be replaced. |
| Change participants | `ChangeParticipant` (new; replaces the public journal sink) | ordered list | Receive the operation's committed-attempt records inside the transaction with an append-only owned-table capability; an exception rolls the operation back. Requires the core writer. |
| Assignment-scope declaration | core declaration value (`#scope-boundary`) | one effective value, merged by layer | Existing precedence and conflict rules; conflicting definitions or plugin-only modes fail compilation; core interprets mode and envelope; the evaluator only narrows. |
| Resource/tenant/scope resolvers | existing `ResourceScopeResolver`, `TenantResolver`, `AssignmentScopeResolver` | keyed / ordered | Produce candidate identities; core verifies tenant and structural identity. |
| Grant fields | existing `Field` declarations | per target | Reserved names (including a new `azg_` prefix) rejected. |
| Module options | typed readonly option object, one per class per panel | keyed by class | Opaque to core except canonical fingerprinting; read with `Panel::options(Class)`; live models, requests, containers and bound closures rejected. |
| Doctor checks | existing `DoctorCheck` | ordered list, unique key | Owned by the contributing source/module; doctor aggregates typed findings. |

Not slots: Laravel events (`AccessEvent` subclasses after root commit, `AccessDecided` when traced) are notification
for applications, not a module bus; the Gate integration; the consumer API.

### What is deliberately not offered

No macros or `__call` on the authorization, panel, change or query API; no untyped option bag; no arbitrary stage
insertion or replacement of a mandatory stage; no module event bus; no service locator for "the module that
provides X"; no sandbox. Extension PHP runs in-process as trusted code: the supported slots cannot bypass core
validation, but nothing prevents trusted code from calling internals or the database directly. Arch tests guard
this package's own modules and Filament; third-party code is guided by markers and contract suites.

### Compilation and sealing

```text
config + panel provider + configurePanels() + attached plugins (deterministic queue)
  -> recorded declarations by layer, each with its origin
  -> per-slot contract checks, closure signature checks, duplicate ids/keys, declaration conflicts
  -> slot requirements (writer for participants, declared alias for RelationSource, scope declaration validity)
  -> source preparation, catalog and role compilation (aliases only for scope bindings)
  -> neutral schema/directory descriptors, writer capabilities
  -> canonical fingerprint (declarations, option objects, handler identities, discovered files)
  -> sealed Panel; registry frozen after application boot
  -> per-operation handler resolution through the container
```

A sealed definition holds scalars, enums, stable references, validated class-strings and immutable option objects;
never container services, request-dependent objects, Eloquent models or executed closure state. A readonly runtime
input may borrow a host model; that input is never cached or serialized as a definition. A code or namespace change
invalidates disposable catalogs and caches, never persisted grant identities.

sections.title: SPI catalogue: purpose, implementer, caller, values, authority, failure
sections.text:
Every implementer or extension-facing contract is listed with the existing behavior that justifies it. Names marked
"new" are indicative; P2 fixes final names and signatures without changing the semantics recorded here.

### Kept, retyped or new contracts

| Contract | Status | Justified by existing behavior | Implementer | Core caller | Values crossing the boundary | Final decision | Failure handling |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `Plugin` | kept, `boot()` removed | panels attach plugins today | apps, modules, packages | panel compiler | `PanelBuilder`, `PluginContext` | compiler | invalid declaration → `DefinitionException`/`PluginConflictException` at boot |
| Source capabilities (`Provides*`, `FencesReads`, `FiltersQueries`, `DescribesSchema`, `ChecksHealth`) | kept | existing sources and contract suites | core adapters, apps | read coordinator, compiler, doctor | refs, envelope `list<AccessScope>`, `EvaluationContext` → definitions/grants/contributions with witnesses; `StateToken` | core pipeline | decision `failed` with source/consistency reason; bounded re-read only for fenced sources |
| `BeforeHook`, `AfterHook`, `ChangePipe` | new names for existing untyped slots | `before()`, `after()`, `changing()` | apps, modules | pipeline / change coordinator | `AccessRequest`, `EvaluationContext`, `Decision`; `Change` + guarded `$next` → `ChangeResult` | core | see slot table |
| `Restriction`, `GrantCondition`, `FiltersAccessQueries` | kept | existing restrictions and SQL predicates | apps, modules | Restriction stage, visibility compiler | request/context/contribution → `RestrictionResult` / `AccessPredicate` | core | failure, or `VisibilityNotSupportedException` for missing exact support |
| `AssignmentScopeDefinition`, `QueryableAssignmentScopeDefinition`, `ResolvedAssignmentScope` | kept in core | roles, `RelationSource`, boundary, writes reference them | Scopes module, apps | boundary, validator, `RelationSource` | ref → resolved ref/tenant/record; fresh structural query; owner tenant | core verification | refusal (exception) → deny/failure; `null` → not accepted |
| `AssignmentScopeEvaluator`, `QueryableAssignmentScopeEvaluator` | new | `ScopeEligibility`, `EligibilityBuilder`, `VisibilityScope` and compile-time `ScopeConfiguration` behavior | Scopes module, apps | boundary/restriction stages, batch, validator, directories, visibility | `AssignmentScopeRuntime`, `ResolvedAssignmentScope`, guarded query | core | `#scope-boundary` |
| `AssignmentScopeDirectory`, `TenantDirectory`, `SubjectDirectory` | kept | UI lookups today | modules, apps | `PanelDirectories` | `LookupContext` → option DTOs | write path revalidates | exception propagates to UI; no write |
| `ProvidesAccessScope`, `ProvidesAssignmentScope`, `ResourceScopeResolver`, typed resource→context mapping | kept + new typed mapping | Gate/visibility resource placement; `method_exists` probe today | host models, apps | boundary, visibility | resource → `AccessScope`; context alias + relation name | core tenant/context checks | mismatch → deny reason; unsupported mapping → `VisibilityNotSupportedException` |
| `TenantResolver`, `AssignmentScopeResolver`, `TenantMembership` | kept, tenancy contracts move namespace | HTTP context selection and membership today | apps, Filament | boundary, tenancy restriction | `Request` → ref; subject + tenant → bool | core | resolver exception → deny `assignment_scope_filter_error` (current mapping) |
| `ChangeParticipant` | new | `AuditPlugin` journal pipe writing in the same transaction | Audit module, apps | write coordinator | list of immutable effective-change records (change, effects, the core-built `AccessEvent` with its `eventId`), operation correlation, `OwnedRowsWriter` | core commits or rolls back | exception rolls back the operation; never swallowed |
| `OwnedRowsWriter` (capability, `#[Spi(kind: Call)]`) | new | `DatabaseSource::appendJournal` inside the active mutation | core only | participants call it | `insert(table base name, list<row>)` for tables the participant declared, on the operation's connection and prefix; rows carry host keys already canonicalized with the public identity helper | core | write outside the call window or to an undeclared/authority table → `UnsupportedDirectWriteException` |
| Storage descriptor + identity-column schema helper | new public read/DDL helpers | audit DDL uses `HostKeyColumns` and private scope constraints today | core | Audit migrations/health, apps | storage id, connection name, prefix, host-key type; column/constraint builders | — | invalid storage → `InvalidConfigurationException` |
| Typed module options | new mechanism | `AuditPlugin::retentionIn()` reads `PanelRecipe` internals | modules, apps | compiler (fingerprint), owners read back | readonly object keyed by its class | owner | non-canonical option value → `DefinitionException` |
| `DoctorCheck` | kept | doctor today | sources, modules | doctor | `DoctorContext` → `DoctorFinding` | doctor aggregation | exception becomes an error finding |
| `Laravel\Console\CommandSupport` + `InvalidCommandInput` (`Spi(Call)`) | new public part of an internal trait | Make, install, stubs and audit-prune commands use `InteractsWithAzGuard::attempt()/selectPanel()` today; exit codes are a frozen CLI contract | module and third-party commands | — | `Closure` body → exit code; options → typed values | core mapping | input errors → `2`, other errors → `1` |
| Config section registration | new, tiny | core root-key validation lists `scaffold` today | module providers | configuration | section name + owner validator | owner | unknown root key → `InvalidConfigurationException` |

### Retired from the supported surface

| Contract | Why | Replacement |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `StoresGrants` as SPI | the write coordinator, `Authorizer`, managers and Filament accept only `DatabaseSource`; the SPI promises an implementable writer that core rejects | core storage is the only authority writer; panels without it are read-only; `PanelSchema` exposes writer capabilities (writable, dynamic permissions) |
| Public `ChangeJournal` sink | it hard-codes the audit table into core; any pipe could write journal rows | `ChangeParticipant` + `OwnedRowsWriter`; the journal is Audit-internal |
| `DependsOnPlugins`, `PluginContext::dependencies()` | sibling-identity dependency | slot requirements checked by core |
| `Plugin::boot()`, `BasePlugin` | no production behavior, second lifecycle route | none |
| `GateMode` | one case, one behavior | the existing `gate.enabled` switch |
| Location-based publication | 97 unmarked types published by directory | explicit attributes (`#api-compatibility`) |

### Neutral contracts sufficient for Filament

Filament today reaches into `DatabaseSource::isDynamic()`, `CurrentContext::get()` and `GateBridge::toGateResult()`.
Targets: writer capabilities in `PanelSchema`; the current scope through `PanelAccess::scope()` (already public);
the Gate result conversion classified as a supported Laravel adapter method. Scope editors are rendered from
`AssignmentScopeTypeSchema`/`AssignmentScopeBindingSchema` and declared directories; Filament never checks for
`azguard/scopes` or imports a module class. No journal UI exists today; adding one later needs a core read contract
implemented by Audit and justified at that time, never a Filament→Audit import or plugin-ID probe.

sections.title: How the complete operation chains work
sections.text:
Each chain names the owner of every step. "Core" means a core coordinator; "extension" means a contributed handler
whose output core verifies. The logical steps below map onto the existing stage graph
`Prepare → Boundary → Before → Authority → Restriction → After`; no stage order or evaluation timing changes.

### A. Building panels

```text
application boot
  core provider: typed config, storages, registry (lazy)        module providers: commands, publish tags, config sections
  panel providers register; configurePanels() callbacks recorded
  per panel, on first use or catalog:cache:
    deterministic plugin queue -> Plugin::register() on a per-panel plugin copy
    -> compile (#extension-system): slot contracts, conflicts, requirements, scope declaration, options
    -> sources prepared, catalog and roles compiled, schema descriptors built
    -> fingerprint over declarations, options, handler identities, discovered files and build id
    -> sealed Panel; after app boot the registry is frozen
```

Multiple panels compile independently; nothing compiled for one panel (options, scope declaration, evaluator
settings) is visible from another. Config caching and `azguard:catalog:cache` store only disposable compiled data
keyed by build id and fingerprint; a stale entry is ignored, never trusted.

### B. Entering a request, job or callback

| Entry | Context handling | Owner |
|:--|:--|:--|
| HTTP `azguard.panel` middleware | admission computes the subject's `AccessScope`; the panel and scope become ambient for the request and are restored in `finally` | core `Laravel`, `Context` |
| Explicit `withinScope()`/`WithinContext` | validates tenant mode, scope mode, declared alias and structural resolution before running the callback; restores in `finally` | core `Context` |
| Request resolvers | tenant/scope resolvers run only when no explicit, resource or ambient value exists; their output is verified like any other ref | core |
| Queued job | only the panel id travels as a hint; the job carries its own refs and is re-authorized; no ambient `AccessScope` is propagated | core `Laravel\Queue` |
| Octane request / queue job lifecycle | scoped bindings (`Authorizer`, `CurrentContext`, `CurrentPanel`, write frames) are flushed per lifecycle by Laravel | Laravel contract (`#evidence`) |
| Fibers | ambient scope, current panel and write-operation frames are stored per Fiber; a Fiber never sees its parent's mutable frame | core |

Extensions never set ambient context; they receive explicit values in their inputs.

### C. One decision

```text
API / model helper / Gate / middleware / Filament
  -> Prepare (core): panel, subject, permission key, captured time
  -> Boundary (core): tenant mode, scope mode, request/resource/ambient/resolver scope, resource tenant and context
       equality, structural verification of a non-global scope; evaluator.allows(common)          [extension: narrow]
  -> Before (extension): Continue or Deny; exception -> failed
  -> Authority (core): read coordinator materializes the envelope once (snapshot per physical handle, fenced
       re-read for FencesReads sources only); code authority modes, grants, roles, global roles, super-admin,
       expiry, policy outcome; each contribution qualified by evaluator.allows(role, contribution) and conditions
  -> Restriction (extension + core): restrictions incl. tenant membership (core) and scope membership (module)
  -> immutable Decision: allow / deny(reason) / failed(kind) / not-applicable
  -> After (extension): observe; optional AccessDecided when traced
```

Infrastructure and contract failures stay distinguishable from ordinary denial (`FailureKind`, reasons, HTTP mapping).
Policy and hook execution never repeats because an authority read retried.

### D. Decision sets

`DecisionSet` prepares inputs once (subject models retained per subject, scopes resolved once per ref, evaluator
answers through `allowsMany`), acquires one snapshot per physical handle and evaluates each decision with chain C.
The subject cap stays; a set whose snapshot or batch answer cannot be established fails as a set. No silent chunking
into different authority states.

### E. Visible lists (`visibleTo`)

```text
inputs (as C) -> selected scope checked against tenant and scope modes
  -> resource mapping: typed resource→context contract (core) when the panel has a scope declaration
  -> candidate contributions read once (FiltersQueries witnesses for database sources)
  -> per contribution: core envelope and expiry checks; branch = guarded resource query
       + eligibleContexts(runtime for this contribution) [extension, exact or unsupported]
       + grant conditions (FiltersAccessQueries) + scope membership predicate + restrictions
  -> core: OR over qualified branches, AND with tenant membership, before-hook predicates, policy deny, tenant guard
  -> confirm the read state; apply to the caller's query
```

SQL NULL handling is explicit; missing exact support raises `VisibilityNotSupportedException` with a stable reason
and never broadens a list. `bounded()` remains the explicit, capped fallback that runs chain C per row. Filament
delegates to this path.

### F. Choosing a target in a UI, then writing

```text
UI -> PanelDirectories: subjects / tenants / scopes(alias) with LookupContext(phase Assignment or Inspection)
   -> declared directory searches; eligibility uses the same evaluator.allows as the write
   -> user submits ids -> describe() revalidates -> chain G performs final validation under the lock
```

A directory is a convenience; the write path never trusts a chosen id.

### G. Changing authority and journaling

```text
host-authorized grant/revoke/sync/update/permission action/role-key migration/touch/reset/expiry prune
  -> core write coordinator: panel writer must be core storage; build/fingerprint pinned
  -> transaction on the writer connection; lock panel_state first; fresh locked reads; captured UTC second; actor
  -> plan Change values; each change: ChangePipe sequence (guarded, once) -> core final validation
       (identity unchanged, tenant, mode, alias, structural verification, evaluator.allows(Assignment, proposed),
        fields, expiry, stale-selection fingerprints) -> writer apply -> effects
  -> core builds AccessEvent values once per effect (eventId ULID, correlation id)
  -> if any effect: ChangeParticipants in order, inside the same transaction, with OwnedRowsWriter
       Audit: one journal row per event, same eventId and payload
  -> root commit: authority state, revisions/epoch and participant rows become durable together
  -> after root commit: dispatch the same event objects; publish eligible cache entries; internal cache invalidation
```

| Case | Result |
|:--|:--|
| No effect (repeat without difference) | no participant call, no row, no event |
| Pipe/validation/participant exception | whole operation rolls back; nothing published |
| Deadlock retry of the root transaction | re-plans from fresh reads, clock, frames and pipes; participants run again; discarded attempts leave no rows or events |
| Operation nested in a host transaction on the same connection | participant rows join the host transaction; events and caches wait for the host's root commit; a host rollback discards everything; no retry inside a nested transaction |
| Storage on a dedicated connection | the host transaction does not cover AzGuard writes (documented existing behavior) |
| Public listener failure after commit | reported; the committed change stays; delivery is best effort |
| Revocation, expiry, touch | never consult the scope evaluator; always available even when scope behavior is removed |

### H. Maintenance

| Operation | Owner | Rule |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Expired-grant prune (`azguard:grants:prune`, scheduler) | core | runs chain G per batch; emits `grant.expired`; participants journal it |
| `azguard:state:reset`, `touch` | core | chain G; `panel.touched` |
| Journal retention (`azguard:audit:prune`) | Audit | reads retention from the panel's `AuditOptions`; deletes old rows in its own short transactions through the core storage descriptor; no authority lock, no revision change, no event |
| Doctor | core aggregator | core checks six authority tables; Audit contributes table presence/shape; Scopes contributes owner/membership warnings |

### I. Activation matrix

| Configuration | Required behavior |
|:--|:--|
| Core only | no scope declaration (`None`), no participant; no module service resolved, no module query, no audit table needed; DevTools commands only in console |
| + Scopes on panel A | panel A interprets its mode and aliases; panel B without the plugin stays `None`; stored scoped rows of B are inert |
| + Audit on panel A | panel A writes journal rows; panel B on the same storage writes none; the audit table is per storage |
| Two panels, different options | different modes/retention per panel; fingerprints differ; no shared mutable option object |
| Module removed after use | data retained; scopes become inert and fail closed; journaling stops; cleanup through revocation/expiry/prune remains |
| Relocated module archive (rehearsal) | the same FQCNs, command names, config keys, event types and migration basenames; no DDL or row change |

sections.title: Persistence: freeze meaning and ownership
sections.text:
Keep schema version 2's authority structure. The redistribution needs **no grant, identity or audit-row rewrite**:
no renamed table or column, no new tenant join, no second grant table. 0.7.0 is tagged and must be assumed installed,
with package-loaded and published migrations, default and named storages.

| Persistent object | Final owner | Rule |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `{prefix}permissions` | core | panel + tenant + name identity, metadata and host-field behavior unchanged |
| `{prefix}role_grants`, `{prefix}permission_grants` | core | tenant/subject/context/origin identity and uniqueness, expiry, actor fields, application columns unchanged; scope behavior moves, the row format does not |
| `{prefix}panel_state`, `{prefix}subject_revisions` | core | incarnation, version, epoch and subject-revision semantics; only the core writer touches them |
| `{prefix}storage_state` | core | schema/codec/storage id/prefix/host-key descriptor; no module writes it; the version stays 2 because no authority structure changes |
| `{prefix}audit_log` | Audit | name, columns, indexes, unique `event_id`, tenant pair constraint, event ids and historical payloads unchanged; installation, shape check, insertion and pruning move together |
| Tenant/scope models and membership | host application | resolved through contracts and stable aliases; no AzGuard table |
| Scopes, DevTools, Filament | none | no table is added for them |

`tenant_*` and `context_*` remain core identity columns even when no scope declaration exists. `context_key = global`
means tenant-wide applicability. Pair constraints preserve the null/global form; disabling scope behavior never
converts scoped rows to global rows.

Frozen together: morph/type aliases, scope type aliases, role/permission keys, source `origin` labels,
`IdentityCodec::VERSION`, the `global` sentinel, host-key canonicalization, lengths, byte/collation semantics, UTC
second timestamps, ULID event and correlation ids, event type strings, event `toArray()` payloads and audit rows.
Moving a PHP class changes none of these. A host class rename keeps its alias.

### Migration identity

Laravel identifies a migration by file basename; a published copy with the same basename is the same migration, and
`publishesMigrations()` rewrites timestamps (`#evidence`). Therefore:

1. The two shipped core basenames (`2026_10_01_000000_create_azguard_storage`,
   `2026_10_09_000000_upgrade_azguard_storage_to_schema_2`) never change, move or get re-dated. Core keeps
   `loadMigrationsFrom` and plain `publishes()` for them.
2. Their bodies delegate to `StorageSchema`, so published copies follow the installed library. After the split,
   `create()` builds six tables and `drop()` drops six tables; this intentional pre-1.0 change is documented in the
   upgrade map because it affects published copies too.
3. Audit ships one new migration with a fixed, later basename (for example
   `2026_10_20_000000_create_azguard_audit_log`), published with plain `publishes()` under its own tag and not
   auto-loaded, so a core-only fresh install has no audit table. Its `up()` creates the table on a storage that lacks
   it, or **adopts** an existing table after verifying its full shape (columns, types, nullability, unique and
   secondary indexes, pair constraint or SQLite triggers, host-key column types); a mismatch fails with an actionable
   message and changes nothing. Its `down()` never drops data: audit data is retained by default.
4. Named storages: core keeps `azguard:storage:migration {name}` (six tables). Audit adds
   `azguard:audit:migration {storage}` generating an application migration from an Audit-owned stub with a distinct
   basename per storage. This replaces the audit tables that 0.7.0 named-storage migrations created through core.
5. Any later schema evolution is a new additive migration owned by the table owner. Changing stored meaning, types
   or identities is a major-version operation. No module alters a core table or another module's table; no
   cross-owner foreign keys.

### Installation and upgrade scenarios (all qualified before the candidate)

| Scenario | Expected result |
|:--|:--|
| Fresh core-only (loaded or published core migrations) | six authority tables; `azguard:doctor` green without an audit table |
| Fresh with Audit on a panel | publish + migrate creates `audit_log` on the default storage; per-storage command for named storages; doctor `audit.table` fails with the exact remedy until then |
| 0.7.0 schema 2, populated, default storage | no core migration pending; the existing `audit_log` keeps working without any step; publishing the Audit migration later only adopts it; zero row changes; checks green |
| 0.7.0 schema 2 with published copies of core migrations | same as above; published copies are not re-run |
| 0.7.0 named storage | its app migration already ran; `audit_log` already exists; Audit adoption per storage when its migration is generated |
| Schema 1 database | existing upgrade path to schema 2; then as above |
| Rollback of the Audit migration | table and rows retained |
| Rollback/teardown of core migrations after the change | six tables dropped; an existing audit table is retained and adoptable |
| Audit or Scopes removed from panels | rows retained; behavior per `#operation-chains` I |

### Health checks

`StorageMigrated` and `StorageHealth` verify only the six core tables and their host-key columns. Audit contributes
`audit.table` (presence on each storage used by an audited panel) and a shape check reusing the storage descriptor.
A core-only installation without `audit_log` is healthy; an audited panel without its table is an error finding.

### Formats that survive the transition

- Event payloads (`AccessEvent::toArray()`) and therefore journal `payload` rows are a frozen machine format. When P2
  makes `StateToken` opaque, the payload keeps exactly the 0.7.0 `state` keys (`knowledge/contracts#tokens`); 0.7.0
  rows and new rows have one shape and are never rewritten.
- FQCNs that hosts may serialize (Kernel values, enums, events, decision values) do not move. Moved types are
  configuration-time or service types; an inventory of serializable types is part of P1 evidence.
- Grant fields: the reserved-name rule gains the `azg_` prefix; P1 checks whether a 0.7.0 application could already
  use such a field, and the upgrade map gives the rename path.
- `meta` stays application grant data, never a module mailbox.
- Disposable catalog/permission caches are keyed by build id, fingerprint and state tokens; serialized class names
  in them are not a persistent contract.

sections.title: What exactly becomes stable
sections.text:
### Publication markers (ecosystem convention)

CoreX, Chatom and Commerz mark their surface with typed attributes: `#[Api(since: …)]` for consumer API and
`#[Spi(kind: Implement|Call, since: …)]` for extension contracts, with `@internal` excluding members (CoreX uses a
`SpiKind` enum, which AzGuard follows for strict typing). AzGuard adopts the
same scheme with its own attribute classes (no runtime dependency on another ecosystem package): `Implement` covers
interfaces and abstract/base classes that extensions implement or extend; `Call` covers capabilities only extensions
call (for example `OwnedRowsWriter`, `PluginContext`, `CommandSupport`). Publication by directory ends; every
supported type carries an attribute, every `@internal` member is excluded, and the generator reads the attributes.

### What becomes stable

| Surface | Decision before 1.0 |
|:--|:--|
| Application entry | Typed `AzGuard\AzGuard` replaces `AzGuardManager`; the facade is a Laravel adapter whose `@method` list is generated from and tested against it; `mixed $subject` becomes a typed union. Established model helpers and `PanelAccess` stay. |
| Consumer vs implementer | Classified by attribute. Implementer promises cover interfaces, abstract bases (`BaseRole`, `PanelProvider`, scope base classes in the module) and declared protected override points. |
| Types and members | Explicit publication; `Internal` namespaces and `@internal` members (constructors "built by the compiler", helpers) excluded. Closing a factory is preferred to deleting a useful type. |
| Named arguments | Parameter names of `#[Api]` methods, constructors and factories are covered: the DSL and value objects are designed for named arguments. A member that does not promise names says `@no-named-arguments`. Core never calls `#[Spi(kind: Implement)]` methods with named arguments, so implementers may rename parameters (PHP binds names to the runtime implementation). |
| Additions | Adding a method to an `Implement` interface or abstract method to a base class, adding a parameter to an overridable method, changing defaults and narrowing accepted types are compatibility breaks after 1.0. Adding methods to final `Api` classes is compatible. |
| Enums | Each public enum is classified **closed** (exhaustive matching supported: `AssignmentScopeMode`, `AssignmentScopePhase`, `BeforeResult`, `Reads`, `StateRefresh`, …) or **open** (may gain cases in minors: `DecisionReason`, `EventType`, `FailureKind`, …). Adding a case to a closed enum is a major change. |
| Shared DTO placement | Clear domain names; module-owned types never appear in core signatures; no generic `Contracts/Values` dump; no interface per DTO. |
| Helpers | Pure Kernel helpers such as `Kernel\Support\Narrow` stay internal unless a supported use exists; modules use supported constructors and validation. `Support\ModelKey` stays public. |
| State evidence | Database/code tokens become opaque public observations with versioned serialization and equality; storage counters and read-session details hidden; no ordering or replica-wait semantics. Event payload keys stay exactly as in 0.7.0 (`knowledge/contracts#tokens`). |
| Decisions | Typed readonly outcomes and contribution lists; HTTP response details are Laravel adapter compatibility. |
| Closed vocabularies | String modes become enums (`TenantMode`, `AssignmentScopeMode`, predicate operations); wire values such as `context_*` stay; the assignment-scope ↔ context terminology mapping is documented. |
| Errors | Domain exceptions and stable `snake_case` codes kept; an inventory fixes class, code and meaning; no removal of meaningful `catch` targets to shrink counts. |
| Configuration and commands | Keys, types, defaults, precedence, environment names, command names/options/exit codes and publish tags frozen. Key paths do not move (`#ownership`). `GateMode` and the `defaults.gate.mode` key are retired in the transition. |
| Events and machine output | Event types/envelopes, doctor finding ids/severities/JSON, explain JSON frozen. `PanelStateTouched` stays public; internal cache invalidation messages stay internal. |
| Models and testing | Supported host customization of grant models and helpers; the consumer fake mirrors `AzGuard\AzGuard`; core and module contract suites are supported SPI tooling; suite fixtures are not. |

### Generator and comparison

The manifest generator must record attributes and kinds, public and protected members with full signatures and
parameter names, constants and values, enum cases with their open/closed class, facade methods derived from the
entry class, PHPDoc generic/class-string contracts of supported members, and module roots. The current manifest
(247 core types: 206 API, 41 SPI; 21 Filament; facade with zero methods; 97 location-published types; 59 core public
methods documented internal) is the 0.7.0 transition baseline, not a target count. A regenerated manifest proves only
freshness; compatibility is a comparison with the frozen candidate and, after 1.0, the previous stable tag
(`#release-gate`). A structural BC checker such as Roave BackwardCompatibilityCheck is an acceptable reference
pattern or dev-only tool for that comparison; the choice is made in P4 and adds no runtime dependency.

### One transition

All namespace, DSL, entry-point, plugin-SPI, slot-typing, token, enum and publication changes form **one documented
pre-1.0 contract transition**, implemented in steps (P2 contracts, P3 relocation) and described by one upgrade map
from 0.7.0. Seeds of that map: Context/Tenancy namespaces; scope DSL → `ScopesPlugin`; module FQCNs for scope
definitions, filters, adapters and membership; `AzGuard\Audit\AuditPlugin`; `ChangeJournal` → participant; retired
`boot()`/`BasePlugin`/`DependsOnPlugins`/`GateMode`/`StoresGrants`; typed hook/pipe contracts; string modes → enums;
`azg_` field prefix; six-table `create()`/`drop()`; Audit migration publishing. After the candidate baseline, only
changes demonstrated necessary by qualification are allowed; naming and API shape are not reopened.

sections.title: Checkable invariants
sections.text:
Each invariant names how it is checked. **Exists** = a check present at 0.7.0 that keeps running; **Build (Pn)** =
a check the named phase creates. P1 introduces every new boundary check in report mode with an explicit, shrinking
allowlist of current violations; an allowlist entry has an owner phase, and all lists are empty at P3 exit.

| # | Invariant | Check | Status |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| I1 | Kernel imports no framework, zone or module code | `ZonesArchTest`, framework-helper scan | Exists |
| I2 | Core references no module: imports, FQCN strings, class-strings, `azguard/<module>` ids, module table names | ownership scan over every autoload root (extends `SourceScan`) | Build (P1) |
| I3 | Modules do not reference each other; Filament references no module; modules reference no Filament | same scan | Build (P1) |
| I4 | Modules, Filament, generated stubs and DevTools output use only attributed symbols and members | member-aware manifest usage test (extends `ApiManifestTest`) | Build (P2) |
| I5 | Every production FQCN has one autoload owner; no `src/Scopes`, `src/Audit`, `src/DevTools`, `src/Plugins/Audit` | autoload/classmap scan, optimized-autoload consumer run | Build (P1 rule, P3 green) |
| I6 | Only the core writer writes authority tables; participants write only declared owned tables during their call | existing direct-write guards and `DirectWritesEngineTest` + capability tests | Exists + Build (P2) |
| I7 | Without a scope declaration non-global requests are denied, scoped rows never apply to global requests, non-global writes are rejected, revocation/expiry still work | scope property tests with no declaration and with a removed plugin over a populated database | Build (P1 harness, P2 green) |
| I8 | Extension outputs only veto, narrow, observe or propose candidates; core verifies tenant, envelope, identity, expiry | `EnginePropertiesTest`, `NegativeFixturesTest`, independent consumer fixture through the same slots | Exists + Build (P2) |
| I9 | Scalar, batch and SQL agree for supported mappings; directory eligibility equals write admission | parity matrix over existing fixtures, module on/off, two panels | Build (P1 harness, maintained P2–P4) |
| I10 | Change pipes continue exactly once, cannot forge the writer result, final validation runs after them | `PipesTest`, `FinalValidationTest` | Exists |
| I11 | One journal row per effective change with the published `eventId`; none for no-op, rollback, nested rollback or discarded retry | `Plugins/Audit` tests, `TransactionPropertiesTest`, `NestedMutationTest`, `ChangeRaceTest` re-targeted to the participant | Exists + Build (P2) |
| I12 | Events and caches are published only after the root commit; listener failure never undoes a commit | `TransactionTest`, `NestedMutationTest` | Exists |
