sections.title: Release gate and permanent architecture rules
sections.text:
1.0 is released only when all conditions hold on one candidate commit, with reproducible evidence linked from P4.

| # | Condition | Proven by |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | **Small core demonstrated.** A basic consumer uses only core API; Scopes and Audit inactive by default; DevTools console-only; core-only boot/check/write resolves no module service, runs no module query and needs no module table; Filament absent from core requirements. | I13, I19, core-only consumer fixture |
| 2 | **Boundaries complete.** No core→module, module↔module or module↔Filament reference; every production file has one owner; empty allowlists. | I2, I3, I5 |
| 3 | **Supported surface closed.** Every supported type/member/override/facade method attributed and classified; signatures and documented generics contain no internal or module-owned type; manifest checks green without exemptions. | I4, I20, manifest generator |
| 4 | **Extension semantics proved.** Built-in modules and an independent consumer fixture use the same slots; invalid contributions, closure signature mismatches, double/skipped continuation, forged writer results, duplicate ids/keys, conflicting declarations and unmet slot requirements fail safely; no supported slot bypasses final validation. | I8, I10, I6, contract suites |
| 5 | **Persistence frozen.** DDL/constraints/collations/host keys match fixtures on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB for core-only and core+Audit; every scenario of `#persistence` passes on populated 0.7.0 fixtures with zero row rewrite. | I15, I16 |
| 6 | **Behavior conserved.** Scalar, batch, visibility, directory and write admission agree, including expiry, NULL, tenant ownership, global/scoped roles, module absent/removed and retained subject-model instances; unsupported capabilities fail closed and are diagnosable. | I7, I9 |
| 7 | **Consistency conserved.** Snapshot/race, dirty-read rejection, nested rollback, retry, after-commit/cache and handle-release suites pass; recorded load/query-budget profiles show no unexplained regression on changed paths. | I11, I12, I21, I22 |
| 8 | **Non-PHP contracts frozen.** Config keys/defaults, environment names, identities/codecs, event/audit payloads, exception codes, commands/options/exit codes, publish tags, doctor/explain JSON and HTTP mapping have fixtures and documentation; 0.7.0 audit rows remain readable as written. | I17 |
| 9 | **Distribution qualified.** Supported PHP/Laravel matrix, database/cache/replica suites, static analysis, style, type coverage, coverage and docs gates pass; core and core+Filament archives work in clean applications as blocking checks; tag release cannot bypass them. | I19, CI |
| 10 | **Freeze operational.** One upgrade map covers the planned break; the candidate becomes the compatibility baseline; after 1.0 CI compares with the previous stable tag and a PR cannot silently replace the baseline. | I18 |

### CI rules: present vs to build

| Rule | Present at 0.7.0 | To build (phase) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Kernel purity | `ZonesArchTest`, `BaselineArchTest` | include new module roots (P1) |
| Ownership, core/module and sibling isolation | partial zone rules | full scan of imports, aliases, grouped imports, FQCN strings, class-strings, plugin ids and table names (P1 report mode, P3 blocking) |
| Supported-symbol usage | Filament class-level check in `ApiManifestTest`, `--check` freshness | attribute-driven, member-aware, modules and stubs included (P2) |
| Authority write ownership | write guards, `FilamentWritesArchTest`, direct-write engine tests | participant capability rules (P2) |
| Activation isolation and inactive cost | — | core-only and module-matrix fixtures with query/resolution assertions (P1 harness, P3 blocking) |
| Sealed definitions, panels, lifecycle | plugin isolation and lifecycle tests, queue tests | two-panel option/declaration fixtures, closure signature rejection (P2) |
| One decision semantics | property tests (engine, scope, transaction), visibility explain tests | parity matrix incl. directories and module on/off (P1, maintained) |
| Transactional journal | audit plugin tests, transaction properties | participant-based variants incl. retry and nested (P2) |
| Schema and formats | DDL fixtures on four drivers, command and config snapshots | populated 0.7.0 fixtures, payload/doctor/explain/exception snapshots (P1) |
| Consumer/distribution | consumer fixture (non-blocking), split/release workflows | blocking consumer job (P1); relocation rehearsal (P4) |
| Post-1.0 compatibility | — | stable-tag comparison for API/SPI and formats, baseline changes only through an explicit release decision (P4) |
| Mutation testing | opt-in workflow | stays opt-in; not a release condition |

sections.title: Transition policy and conditional physical extraction
sections.text:
### Order: evidence, contracts, relocation, freeze (D12)

Revision 1 changed installers and audit ownership in P1, before the participant contract (P2) and the Audit module
(P3) existed, so P1 could not "move installation, health checking, insertion and pruning together". Revision 2 orders
the work so each step has its owner and its safety net:

| Phase | Purpose | Production behavior change |
|:--|:--|:--|
| P1 Baseline evidence and compatibility harness | capture 0.7.0 formats, populated databases, manifests and parity results; add boundary scans in report mode; make the archive consumer check blocking | none (tests and CI only) |
| P2 Contract transition in place | introduce the final supported surface and make existing scope, audit and generator code use it from its current location | yes: the single documented API/SPI transition |
| P3 Relocate modules and split ownership | move complete slices into module roots, split schema/installer/health/config ownership, consolidate internal coordinators | yes: FQCNs of moved types, installer split |
| P4 Qualify the candidate and freeze | close the release gate on one candidate commit and make compatibility comparison permanent | none beyond fixes demonstrated by qualification |

Each phase leaves `main` releasable as a 0.x version with all existing suites green. Phase detail sessions may split
work into items but may not move a responsibility across phases without an explicit plan amendment.

### Conditional future relocation

Physical extraction is outside the required phases. An internal module is relocation-ready when I2–I5, I13, I16 and
I19 hold. Relocating one is an owner distribution decision under principle 3 and needs its own plan: the new archive
takes the same PSR-4 prefix and provider while the base package drops them (one autoload owner); FQCNs, commands,
config sections, publish tags, event types, migration basenames and populated data are unchanged; Composer
requirements document the new dependency. Licensing cannot introduce a second engine or schema.

### Artifacts to author during phase detail (one owner each)

| Artifact | Phase |
|:--|:--|
| Recorded now: `knowledge/type-map`, `knowledge/target-structure`, `knowledge/contracts`, `knowledge/identities`, `knowledge/upgrade-map` (seed), raw inventory and generators in `artifacts/inventory/` | design (revision 2) |
| Populated 0.7.0 database fixtures, DDL fixtures, snapshots of every identity in `knowledge/identities`, serializable-FQCN list, 0.7.0 manifest snapshot, parity harness, boundary scans driven by `artifacts/inventory/target-map.json` with allowlists | P1 |
| Member-level inventory (public/protected members, overrides, named-argument stance) on top of the type map; implementation of `knowledge/contracts`; complete upgrade map | P2 |
| Module activation matrix fixtures, relocated module trees, Audit migration/adoption/named-storage chain, config section registration | P3 |
| Candidate and stable-tag baselines, recorded load/race evidence, relocation rehearsal, release notes | P4 |

Do not add implicit panels, consistency profiles, subject-level write locks, a replica freshness receipt, distributed
transactions, external audit delivery, a journal UI or a general plugin workflow engine. Those keep their roadmap status.

sections.title: Cost of the architecture
sections.text:
The architecture must not cost more concepts than it removes. Counts are of supported concepts, not classes.

### Supported concepts added and removed

| Added | Removed or narrowed |
|:--|:--|
| `AssignmentScopeEvaluator` (+ optional exact-query capability) | `AssignmentScopeFilter`, `AssignmentScopeAccessAdapter`, `AssignmentScopeMembership`, `ConfigurableAssignmentScopeDefinition` leave the core SPI (module-owned) |
| `AssignmentScopeMode`, `TenantMode` enums | string modes |
| scope declaration slot | `PanelBuilder::scopes(AssignmentScopePolicy)` (DSL moves to `ScopesPlugin`) |
| `ChangeParticipant` + `OwnedRowsWriter` | public `ChangeJournal`, `StoresGrants` as SPI |
| `BeforeHook`, `AfterHook`, `ChangePipe` names for existing slots | duck-typed `handle()`, name-injected invocation |
| typed module options, config section registration | `AuditPlugin::retentionIn(PanelRecipe)` introspection, core knowledge of `scaffold` |
| typed resource→context mapping contract | `method_exists` probe |
| storage descriptor + identity-column helper | private DDL duplication pressure |
| `#[Api]`/`#[Spi]` attributes | location-based publication |
| `AzGuard\AzGuard` entry | `AzGuardManager` + facade-only signatures |
| — | `Plugin::boot()`, `BasePlugin`, `DependsOnPlugins`, `PluginContext::dependencies()`, `GateMode` |

Net: the implementer surface becomes smaller and every remaining slot has one named contract.

### What each audience must do

| Audience | Required action |
|:--|:--|
| Basic application (no tenants/scopes/audit) | update imports of moved Context/Tenancy types if used; remove `defaults.gate.mode` from a published config; nothing else |
| Tenancy users | `Tenancy`/`Contracts\Tenancy` imports |
| Scope users | attach `ScopesPlugin` instead of `->scopes(AssignmentScopePolicy…)`; module FQCNs for definitions, filters, adapters, membership; models use the typed mapping contract or keep `ContextAware` |
| Audit users | `AzGuard\Audit\AuditPlugin`; existing installs need no database step; fresh installs publish one migration (and run the per-storage command for named storages) |
| Plugin authors | drop `boot()`/`BasePlugin`/`DependsOnPlugins`; implement named slot contracts; journal through `ChangeParticipant` |
| Custom writer authors | none supported before either; read sources unchanged |
| Filament users | upgrade both packages together (`self.version`) |
| Generator users | none: command names and `scaffold` keys unchanged |

### Runtime cost

Core-only: no scope evaluator, no participant, one fewer table, no module providers doing work. With modules: the
same queries as 0.7.0 on the same paths; evaluator calls replace direct `ScopeEligibility` calls one-for-one;
participant inserts replace pipe inserts one-for-one. P4 confirms with recorded load profiles (I22).

sections.title: Residual risks and trade-offs
sections.text:
Residual risks and deliberate trade-offs. Each has an owner phase and a stop condition.

| Risk / trade-off | Why accepted or how contained | Owner |
|:--|:--|:--|
| The exact-query split for scopes (`eligibleContexts`) is the most intricate move: today `VisibilityScope` mixes structural mapping, owner checks, bounded materialization and per-record branches. | P1 parity harness first; P2 moves only behind an unchanged parity matrix; any case that cannot be expressed exactly stays `unsupported`, never approximate. Stop if parity drops. | P1, P2 |
| Removing the panel lock from journal pruning changes lock interaction on MySQL/MariaDB (`(panel, occurred_at)` range deletes next to inserts). | Deletes by selected ids in short transactions; P3 runs the engine race suites with concurrent writes and prune on every driver; if deadlocks appear, prune retries its own batch (no authority lock). | P3 |
| Published copies of core migrations change effective `create()`/`drop()` behavior. | Intended, documented; teardown retains the audit table; populated fixtures cover published copies. | P1, P3 |
| Fresh installs with Audit need one publish step (named storages one command each). | Same model as other audit packages; doctor names the remedy; avoids an audit table in every core-only install. | P3 |
| Signature break for every third-party plugin/pipe/hook. | Pre-1.0, once, with an upgrade map; `register()` signature unchanged; closures still accepted for single-method slots. | P2 |
| Retiring `StoresGrants` closes a door nobody can use today. | A future custom writer needs its own design against the write coordinator (rationale in D10); not reopened before 1.0. | P2 |
| Attribute markers on ~250 types is a large mechanical change. | Generator-assisted; P1 snapshot of the 0.7.0 manifest makes every publication change reviewable. | P2 |
| In-process extensions are trusted PHP. | No sandbox is promised; supported slots cannot bypass validation; arch tests protect this repository's own modules only. | — |
| Config section registration adds a small mechanism. | Needed so core holds no module literal while keeping strict unknown-key validation; limited to root sections. | P3 |
| Opaque `StateToken` serialization interacts with frozen event payloads. | Either keep existing payload keys or add an encoding discriminator; never reinterpret 0.7.0 rows. Decided once in P2. | P2 |
| A third-party scope type alongside the module's types needs the module's access adapters, because the evaluator slot is single-valued. | Matches today (adapters are already the external-scope mechanism); a second evaluator would mean two eligibility semantics. | — |
| D5 internal consolidation of the read coordinator can disturb consistency timing. | Required for 1.0 only to remove concrete-source branches from decision and query semantics; further restructuring is optional and gated by I21/I22. | P3 |

sections.title: Independent review record (revision 2)
sections.text:
Independent review of revision 1, 2026-10-10, by Claude Opus 5.5 (xhigh effort) on the owner's request. Method: read
the plan through `plan.py`; read the code paths behind every boundary (plugins, compiler, scopes in boundary/frame/
visibility/validator/directories/admission, change pipeline and journal, storage schema/health/migrations, provider,
configuration, commands, Filament imports, CI workflows, manifests); compared with CoreX, Chatom, Commerz and Vaulter;
checked external premises in primary sources (`#evidence`). No code, database, commit or push; no review or execution
process was started.

### Confirmed from revision 1 (kept)

One engine/visibility compiler/write coordinator; internal modules Scopes, Audit, DevTools and the separate Filament
package; installation ≠ activation; panel-local sealed contributions; core-owned identity columns; no grant-data
migration; Audit owning its table with full-shape adoption; same-transaction journaling with core-built event ids;
after-commit publication; no public `StorageMutation`; deep internal authority reads (D5); one pre-1.0 transition with
a frozen candidate and stable-tag comparison (D4); conditional physical extraction (D6); no macros, bus or sandbox.
Verified facts: 247/206/41 core and 21 Filament manifest types, zero facade methods, single-case `GateMode`,
non-blocking consumer fixture, `StorageSchema` creating and dropping `audit_log`, `AuditPlugin::retentionIn` reading
`PanelRecipe`, Filament importing `Scopes\{AssignmentScopePhase,CurrentContext}`.

### Changes and reasons

| # | Finding in revision 1 | Change in revision 2 | Where |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| R1 | Inheritance assigned to the module; one broad evaluator for resolution, applicability, admission, resource mapping and descriptions. Mode is interpreted in `EvaluationFrame::sourceScopes`, `Visibility`, `BoundaryStage`, `PanelAdmission`, `ChangeValidator`, i.e. over core columns in every path. | Core owns the algebra (closed mode enum, envelope, structural verification); the evaluator only answers eligibility (scalar, batch, exact SQL). Resolution stays on the existing definition contract. Explicit call-site map and failure mapping. | D7, `#scope-boundary` |
| R2 | `StoresGrants` is published SPI with contract tests, but the write coordinator, `Authorizer`, managers and Filament accept only `DatabaseSource`. | Authority writes are core storage only; the SPI is retired; panels expose writer capabilities. | D10, `#spi-catalog` |
| R3 | Filament leaks not enumerated (`DatabaseSource::isDynamic`, `CurrentContext::get`, `GateBridge::toGateResult`). | Neutral replacements named. | `#spi-catalog` |
| R4 | `Plugin::boot()` kept although only tests observe it; `DependsOnPlugins` replaced by an unspecified capability-requirement API. | `boot()`/`BasePlugin` retired (ecosystem plugins are declaration-only); requirements are implied by slots and checked by core; `register()` signature unchanged. | D8 |
| R5 | Untyped slots: duck-typed pipes, before/after hooks invoked by parameter name through `RuntimeInvoker`. | One named contract per slot; closures only for single-method contracts with compile-time signature checks. | D8, `#extension-system` |
| R6 | Audit participant timing, capability scope and journal API removal unspecified; capability described as "mutation". | Participants run once per operation after the last effect, inside the transaction; capability is append-only to declared tables; public `ChangeJournal` retired. | D8, `#operation-chains` G |
| R7 | Migration identity not addressed: Laravel keys migrations by basename and `publishesMigrations()` re-dates files; named storages got `audit_log` through core; `StorageMigrated` requires `audit_log`. | Basename rules, Audit migration with a new fixed basename, non-destructive `down()`, per-storage Audit command, six-table health. | D11, `#persistence` |
| R8 | P1 split installers and audit ownership before the participant contract and the Audit module existed. | Phases reordered: evidence → contracts in place → relocation → freeze. | D12, `#transition-policy` |
| R9 | `azguard:install` imports scaffolding and calls `azguard:make:panel`; core config validates `scaffold` keys. | Onboarding command owned by DevTools under the same name; module config sections registered by their owners; key paths unchanged. | D7, `#ownership` |
| R10 | Publication markers and named-argument policy unspecified; ecosystem uses `#[Api]`/`#[Spi(kind)]`; PHP binds named arguments to the runtime implementation. | Attribute markers; covered parameter names for API; positional core calls into implementer SPI; open/closed enums. | D9, `#api-compatibility` |
| R11 | Release gate did not distinguish existing checks from checks to build. | Invariants I1–I22 with status and owner phase; gate conditions reference them. | `#invariants`, `#release-gate` |
| R12 | Generic "source lifecycle capability" proposed for `RelationSource` binding. | Core-internal preparation of a core adapter; no new public SPI. | D7 |
| R13 | `method_exists` resource→context probe and the `FolderSource` branch in visibility. | Typed mapping contract; neutral contribution property. | `#scope-boundary` |
| R14 | Revisions 1 and 2 fixed boundaries as rules and a map of mixed areas only (~40 classes); detail sessions would have re-derived placement for the remaining types. | Exhaustive per-type map generated from code (464 + 43 rows), package/module trees, normative signatures, identity inventory and upgrade-map seed; structure rule D13. | `knowledge/type-map`, `knowledge/target-structure`, `knowledge/contracts`, `knowledge/identities`, `knowledge/upgrade-map` |
| R15 | DevTools and Audit commands depend on the internal console trait for exit codes and panel selection; published migrations and generated storage migrations call `Storage\Schema\StorageSchema` by FQCN; role-binding filters are validated at compile time by `ScopeConfiguration` from `RoleCompiler`. | `CommandSupport` becomes a supported `Spi(Call)` trait; `StorageSchema` FQCN and `create/drop/upgrade` frozen; `AssignmentScopeEvaluator::validate()` keeps compile-time failure. | `#spi-catalog`, `knowledge/contracts` |

### Superseded decisions

D1 → D7 (ownership, scope algebra, writer and DevTools details). D2 → D8 (plugin SPI, typed slots, participant).
D3, D4, D5, D6 stay accepted; D9 and D11 refine D4 and D3 without contradicting them; D10, D12 and D13 are new.

### Not changed on purpose

Filament stays one package; no package per module; Folder/Gate/Relation sources stay in core; tenant isolation stays
in core; Audit remains same-transaction; no outbox, implicit panel, consistency profile or per-subject lock.

stable morph aliases, after-commit envelopes, condition-specific errors, command conventions and consumer suites.
Keep AzGuard's own domain vocabulary and do not add a runtime dependency on another ecosystem package merely
to share style.
